full_judgment: 11.It was contended that the legislative powers conferred  by the Proclamation on the President designated by it was not intended to extend to changing the system of Government or to the making of a constitutional piece of legislation, even of an interim nature. It will, however, be seen that in addition to conferring on the President  all other powers including the executive powers, the Proclamation, after having noticed the prevailing circumstances invested him with all the "Legislative powers of the Republic". Obviously, the expression "Legislative powers of the Republic" is of the widest amplitude and admits of no limitation. The Proclamation, in our view, empowered the President designated by it to make any law or legal provision, even of a constitutional nature. We looked for but found no indication in the Proclamation to the contrary. On the other hand, assurance is lent to this view by the further provision in the Proclamation which empowered the President to do everything necessary to give the people of Bangladesh an orderly and just Government, including the power to appoint a Prime Minister and other Ministers. The impugned clauses (5) to (8) of the Provisional Constitution Order were thus authorised by the terms of the Proclamation.
